title: Direct image, derived limits, and completeness
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Fix the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $A$ is a commutative Noetherian ring, $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, $A/I$ is additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ is finite and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$. For $T=X,Y$ put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and use $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ and its strict tower category. Use the canonical coefficient identification $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] and the ordinary uncompleted operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. In this statement $\Rlim$ means the total right derived inverse-limit functor on strict towers of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], whose values have the derived-limit property of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. Derived $I$-completeness means that the Koszul completion unit of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is invertible; its canonical identification with quotient-tower completion is [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction]. All $P_n$ tensors on $T$ mean tensors over $A_T$ with $(P_n)_T$, with the resulting complex restricted to $A_T$-modules when used in a tower.

Levelwise direct image on tower categories has a total right derived functor

$$
 Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}:
 D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(X))
 \longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(Y)),
$$

with $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\simeq Rf_*M_n$.
For every $M_\bullet$ the canonical map

$$
 Rf_*\Rlim M_\bullet
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \Rlim\bigl(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. Under the two canonical Roos triangles associated with the
derived inverse-limit [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] construction, it
is induced by the canonical isomorphisms

$$
 Rf_*R\!\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{\sim}
 R\!\prod_nRf_*M_n
$$

and their commutation with $(1-s)$. If $K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ is derived
$I$-complete, then $Rf_*K$ is derived $I$-complete. For every $n\geq1$, the
projection-formula morphism

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\longrightarrow Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)
$$

is a functorial isomorphism

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)=Rf_*K_n,
$$

and these isomorphisms commute with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$. Under them, the
completion map for $Rf_*K$ is the composite

$$
 Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\Rlim K_\bullet
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet.
$$

Here the canonical inverse-limit comparison is the derived comparison of the underived equality $f_*\lim=\lim f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$, computed on K-injective strict towers. The finite-level projection isomorphisms are evaluations of the projection-formula mate on the ringed diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with quotient diagram $((P_n)_T)_n$. Thus the completion identification uses that specified morphism of derived strict towers, including its reduction unit, rather than just a family of evaluated morphisms.

Stacks Tag 0A07 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim) supplies the ringed-topos derived-limit argument. Tag 099N (proetale.tex, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case) gives preservation of derived completeness and reconstruction for constant Noetherian coefficients. The completed-coefficient version here uses the indicated coefficient comparison, perfect projection formula and Koszul reconstruction; no identification with constant $A$-module sheaves is asserted.

proof.text: The finite quotient rings $P_n$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Its comparison $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ and its equations for the quotient projections give exactly the ring identification required by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. In particular the module inverse image $f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to the additive module direct image $f_*$. Apply these functors levelwise to strict towers; the adjunction restricts to compatible families of maps, and exactness is levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Thus the tower inverse image is exact and left adjoint to levelwise direct image.

source.place: First sentence: coefficient identification and tower functors

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] the tower categories are Grothendieck abelian. Choose functorial K-injective resolutions $C_\bullet\to J_\bullet$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence]. The additive functor $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ applied termwise preserves chain homotopies, shifts, finite sums and the matrices of mapping cones [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so it induces an exact functor from the homotopy category to the target derived category. The theorem [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] constructs its total right derived functor, computed by $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}J_\bullet$.

source.place: First sentence: existence of the total right derived tower functor

proof.text: Evaluation of $J_\bullet$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective]. Evaluation preserves quasi-isomorphisms, since kernels, cokernels and hence cohomology are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Therefore $C_n\to J_n$ is a K-injective resolution and $f_*J_n$ computes $Rf_*M_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. The comparison $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\cong Rf_*M_n$ is induced by these same resolutions. All transitions are the evaluated maps of $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}J_\bullet$, so the comparisons respect them.

By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], both $f_*$ and $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ preserve K-injective complexes. Let $\Delta$ be the constant-tower functor. It is exact by levelwise exactness. The termwise inverse limit is right adjoint to $\Delta$: a map into the limit is precisely a compatible family. The same K-injective-preservation lemma implies that $\lim J_\bullet$ is K-injective. Consequently $Rf_*\Rlim M_\bullet$ is computed by $f_*\lim J_\bullet$, while $\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet$ is computed by $\lim f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}J_\bullet$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Underived $f_*$ commutes with this limit: for every module $H$, the adjunction identifies maps $H\to f_*\lim J_n$ with compatible maps $f^*H\to J_n$, and thence with maps $H\to\lim f_*J_n$. The resulting chain isomorphism defines the canonical natural comparison $a_M$. K-injective comparison [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] makes it independent of resolution and natural in the derived tower.

source.place: Tag 0A07, label lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim; explicit strict-resolution form using the exact identified-coefficient inverse image

proof.text:
For $H\in D(Y_{\Proet},A)$ the adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the product property in [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] give
$\operatorname{Hom}(H,Rf_*R\!\prod M_n)=\operatorname{Hom}(Lf^*H,R\!\prod M_n)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(Lf^*H,M_n)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(H,Rf_*M_n)$.
Thus the map whose $n$-th component is $Rf_*p_n$ is the canonical product isomorphism $\alpha$. It is natural because each displayed bijection is natural.

Set $P=\prod_nJ_n$. Each $J_n$ is K-injective by step 3. The theorem [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] says $P$ is K-injective and represents the derived product; apply it also to the K-injectives $f_*J_n$ from step 4. Products exist here by [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. The ordinary right-adjoint product isomorphism $f_*P\cong\prod_nf_*J_n$ has components $f_*p_n$, hence represents $\alpha$ of step 5. For the shift maps, $p_ns=t_{n+1,n}p_{n+1}$ and $p'_ns'=f_*(t_{n+1,n})p'_{n+1}$. Composing with every $p'_n$ shows $s'\alpha=\alpha f_*s$; additivity gives the equality for $1-s$. This is the required actual chain-level square.

source.place: Roos comparison sentence: product models and shift square

proof.text: Countable products of $A_T$-modules are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], and the module categories are Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], hence have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Thus [lem-weil-derived-limit-roos-complex] applies to $J_\bullet$ and $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}J_\bullet$: it identifies their termwise limits with the shifted cones of $1-s$. The shifted cone of a map between K-injectives is K-injective: its Hom complex from an acyclic complex is, up to the cone signs, the shifted cone of a map between two acyclic Hom complexes, so is acyclic by its degreewise split cone sequence [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All products in this assertion are K-injective by step 6. Hence these cone models compute the derived functors by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. The chain square in step 6 induces their cone isomorphism, since additive $f_*$ preserves the two finite cone summands and cone differential. The map $\lim J\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of [lem-weil-derived-limit-roos-complex] has components $(0,\iota)$, so this cone isomorphism agrees with $a_M$ of step 4 under those quasi-isomorphisms. This also checks the connecting arrows, rather than merely filling a square of abstract triangles. It proves the claimed compatibility with both canonical Roos triangles.

source.place: Roos comparison sentence: cone isomorphism including boundary maps

proof.text: For each $n$, apply [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] with the given finite perfect $P_n$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\pi_n:(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{A_Y}(P_n)_Y\to Rf_*K_n$ and explicitly gives its compatibility with quotient tower maps. Its map is the counit-tensor mate of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. No completeness hypothesis is needed for these finite-level isomorphisms.

source.place: Final sentence: finite-level perfect projection formula

proof.text: To retain strict-tower coherence, use the ringed diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] for $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, with ring diagram $\Delta A_T$. The functors of step 1 are a morphism of these ringed topoi: their set-sheaf adjunction is componentwise and inverse image preserves finite limits componentwise. Put $Q_{T,\bullet}=((P_n)_T)_n$. Apply the general projection mate of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] on these sites to $E=\Delta K$ and $Q_{Y,\bullet}$. This is a morphism in the derived category of strict towers. The reduction construction in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] is $\Delta K\otimes^L Q_{X,\bullet}$: if $P$ is K-flat representing $K$, then $\Delta P$ is K-flat for diagram tensor, since tensor and acyclicity are levelwise, and its tensor with $Q_\bullet$ is exactly the specified reduction complex. Pullback of $Q_{Y,\bullet}$ is $Q_{X,\bullet}$ by the quotient equations of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image].

source.place: Final sentence: specified strict-tower projection mate

proof.text: The constant-tower functor also preserves K-injectives. Indeed $\operatorname{ev}_1$ is its exact left adjoint: a map $N_\bullet\to\Delta V$ is uniquely determined by $N_1\to V$, with other components obtained using $N_n\to N_1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] and [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Thus a K-injective resolution $K\to I$ gives the resolution $\Delta K\to\Delta I$, and $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}\Delta K=\Delta Rf_*K$ under the canonical resolution identifications. With this identification, the mate in step 9 is a map $\Pi_K:(Rf_*K)_\bullet\to Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$. Evaluation is exact inverse image on the diagram sites, and its tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Consequently evaluating this counit-tensor construction gives exactly $\pi_n$ of step 8 (evaluation of the counit is its counit, using the same tower resolution as step 3). Every evaluation of its cone is acyclic by step 8; levelwise cohomology [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] makes its cone zero. Hence $\Pi_K$ is a strict derived-tower isomorphism.

source.place: Final sentence: constant comparison and detection of the strict projection isomorphism

proof.text:
Let $u_K:\Delta K\to K_\bullet$ denote the strict reduction unit. Naturality in the coefficient argument and the unit normalization $\alpha_{\Delta A_Y}=1$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied on the diagram sites to $\Delta A_Y\to Q_{Y,\bullet}$, give the equality
$\Pi_K\,u_{Rf_*K}=Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}(u_K)$,
where the right-hand source is identified with $\Delta Rf_*K$ as in step 10. This is an equality of strict derived-tower morphisms. Apply $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. On constant towers its value is the original object: the K-injective representative $\Delta I$ has limit $I$. The comparison $a_{\Delta K}$ in step 4 is the identity under these identifications, since the ordinary limit comparison on a constant tower is the identity. Naturality of $a$ for $u_K$ therefore gives
$R\lim(\Pi_K)\circ\operatorname{comp}_{Rf_*K}=a_{K_\bullet}\circ Rf_*(\operatorname{comp}_K)$.
Here the completion units are those induced by the strict quotient maps in [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction]. This proves the asserted unit compatibility without assuming evaluation is faithful on morphisms.

source.place: Final sentence: compatibility with the completion unit

proof.text: If $K$ is derived $I$-complete, [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] says $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is an isomorphism. In the equality of step 11, its right-hand side is an isomorphism by step 4, and $R\lim(\Pi_K)$ is an isomorphism by step 10. Therefore $\operatorname{comp}_{Rf_*K}$ is an isomorphism. The identity $c_{Rf_*K}\circ\kappa_{Rf_*K}=\operatorname{comp}_{Rf_*K}$ with $c_{Rf_*K}$ invertible from [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] makes its Koszul completion unit invertible. By [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], $Rf_*K$ is derived $I$-complete. Step 11 is exactly the displayed completion composite under the projection isomorphism, and step 8 supplies all transition compatibilities.

source.place: Final sentence: completeness and the specified completion composite

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q06-314f4411d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 12 steps and the full statements of all 24 cited nodes; the delivery adds no new nodes. Sources checked: the current blueprint proof (main-20261015, sk-prop-pbc-complete) and the Stacks entries 0A07 (sites-cohomology lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, which uses the same diagram-site argument as steps 9-10) and 099N (proetale lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case, constant coefficients; the item's corrected note is accurate). The statement correction only introduces objects the old text used without defining: the adic datum's hypotheses exactly, the completed coefficient sheaf A_T, the canonical identification f^{-1}A_Y=A_X and the functorial strict-tower Rlim. It adds no hypothesis and keeps every displayed clause, so nothing is weakened. Each step's hypotheses were checked against the cited statements: exact f^* and its adjunction; Grothendieck tower category with functorial K-injectives; the total-derived lemma; evaluation preserving K-injectives; right adjoints of exact functors preserving K-injectives for f_*, f_*^Tow and lim; products of K-injectives; the Roos lemma's exact products and enough injectives via the countable-products, Grothendieck and enough-injectives nodes; the perfect projection formula on the same datum; the projection mate on the diagram sites with ev_1 left adjoint to the constant tower; unit naturality and the normalization alpha_{R_Y}=1 giving the completion-unit equality before Rlim; and c kappa = comp for completeness. Small cases tested: f=id, K=0, I=A, I=0 with r=0, and Z_p with I=(p). Duplicate candidate lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison is re-derived in steps 2-4 rather than cited; this creates no node, so it is not a fault. Only step 5 is marked elementary, and it is. No cycle; proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. The declared tool_uses are all generic and accepted; the off-route ones are countable-products-exact and ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian. No SGA. The item has a stage-2 Lean record, so it may need a stage-2 recheck against the clarified statement. No fixes.

proof.text:
The tower category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] is Grothendieck
abelian with exact evaluation functors, so levelwise K-injective resolutions
(also with respect to the K-injective presentation of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]) give the total right derived functor
$Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ with
$\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\simeq Rf_*M_n$.
Applying $Rf_*$ to the canonical Roos triangle of
[prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] for $M_\bullet$ and comparing with the Roos
triangle for $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet$, using that the derived
products commute with $Rf_*$ (they are the products of the levelwise
K-injective resolutions and direct image is a right adjoint, hence
product-preserving) and with $(1-s)$, identifies the two triangles and gives
the displayed isomorphism $Rf_*\Rlim M_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Rlim(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet)$. If $K$ is derived $I$-complete
then, applied to the tower $K_\bullet$, this shows $Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Rlim Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$, so $Rf_*K$ is derived
$I$-complete; [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] supplies the
projection-formula isomorphisms
$(Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(K\otimes_A^LP_n)=Rf_*K_n$ of
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map], commuting with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ by the
normalization data of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; under them the
completion map for $Rf_*K$ is the displayed composite.
